items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: Kenny Clark I think did quite a few recordings with her at this time... I -- when I came out of the army I got the 52nd Street jazz, with Kenny Clark, Fats Navarro, Sonny Stitt.

ctx.x: And I might add that during this same time I was doing quite a bit of recording with Mildred Bailey. She kept -- she always wanted Roy, Teddy Wilson and myself with her. It's a marvelous dates because we did some things with I think the writer was Alec Wilder, and she did some very good things during this time. And we used to have some great parties at our house. She loved to give parties and have all the musicians over. And Kenny Clark@ I think did quite a few recordings with her at this time. Also --

items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: this is when they had Don Biase and Roy and Georgia Ali, I think I mentioned that, Kenny Clarke, and Jimmie Hamilton.

ctx.x: Red Allen, yeah. And we would play dirty hearts, or sometimes rehearsal would start three hours late, we'd start playing hearts. But very memorable times. Most of the guys are dead now. Let's see, Tyree's dead, isn't he. Yeah. Red. Yeah. And yeah, we recorded during that time with -- I think it was during -- no, this was after. I'm getting confused because I worked with him before the war, this is when we did those things with Billie Holiday -- with Don Redman and the band. This is when they had Don Biase and Roy…

We've been here looking through a stack of jazz books, and a stack of records (inaudible). It's rather upsetting. In all of the books that we found, you don't find any reference to John Collins. Yet there's a rather detailed personnel of bands that you played in. Isn't that strange?
